sentences.text: Eastmanosteus is a fossil genus of placoderms, an extinct class of armored fish, belonging to the group Dunkleostea.
These were medium-to-large fish, with some specimens reaching nearly 3 meters in total length.
Complete exoskeletons with preserved soft-tissue traces of E. calliaspis from Australia make this species one of the best-known dunkleosteids.
The genus Eastmanosteus was described by Obruchev in 1964.
The type species of the genus Eastmanosteus is Dinichthys pustulosus.
Eastmanosteus and its relative Dunkleosteus belong to the family Dunkleosteidae.
The time range for Eastmanosteus is from the Givetian to the Frasnian, approximately 387.95 to 375.2 million years ago.
Eastmanosteus fossils are found in marine sediments from the Middle to Late Devonian periods across many parts of the world.
E. calliaspis fossils come from the Frasnian Gogo Formation in northwestern Western Australia.
E. licharevi is a poorly known species from Russia, with material from the Frasnian and Famennian periods.
E. lundarensis is a medium-sized species from the Eifelian period of south-central Manitoba, Canada.
E. pustulosus was a large, widely distributed form found in the Middle-Late Devonian of the United States and the Frasnian of Poland.
E. yunnanensis is from the Middle Devonian of Yunnan Province, China.
An undescribed species of Eastmanosteus is based on material from the Frasnian of Kerman, east Iran.
A 2016 study suggests that the status of Dunkleosteidae as a clade separate from Dunkleosteoidea is in doubt.
